hypothesis.required_relation: Output is the sorted list with the same multiplicity of each integer as in xs.
hypothesis.actual_relation: The return expression first converts xs to a set, removing duplicates, and then sorts the distinct values.
hypothesis.trigger: Any xs with a repeated value, such as [2, 2], produces a shorter result than required.
hypothesis.alternative: For inputs without duplicates the results coincide, as in the public base example.
hypothesis.reason: The set conversion discards occurrence counts, while the specification explicitly requires preserving them.

tests.reason: Repeated-value lists directly distinguish multiplicity preservation from set deduplication.

hypothesis.required_relation: Return True exactly when every value in required belongs to container; additional container values are permitted.
hypothesis.actual_relation: Returns whether the sets of the two arguments are equal, requiring both containment directions.
hypothesis.trigger: Use a container with an extra value absent from required, while all required values are present.
hypothesis.alternative: When the two lists have the same distinct values, this equality agrees with the stated membership condition.
hypothesis.reason: Set equality rejects extras in container even though the specification explicitly allows them.

tests.reason: The first case isolates the forbidden requirement that container have no extra distinct values; the second checks duplicates do not affect membership.

hypothesis.required_relation: Return True exactly when sum(xs) <= limit, regardless of the length of xs.
hypothesis.actual_relation: Returns False immediately when len(xs) > 2; otherwise returns whether sum(xs) <= limit.
hypothesis.trigger: A list longer than two whose sum is at most limit is incorrectly rejected.
hypothesis.alternative: For lists of length at most two, the sum comparison implements the stated relation.
hypothesis.reason: The unconditional length cutoff imposes a restriction absent from the specification and can change the result.

tests.reason: A length-three list with an allowed sum exposes the cutoff; the length-two case checks the ordinary comparison path.

hypothesis.required_relation: Return the first suitable value from xs.
hypothesis.actual_relation: Returns the first element when xs is nonempty and None when it is empty.
hypothesis.trigger: The meaning of suitable is unspecified, so no input can be shown from the prompt alone to require a value other than the first element or None.
hypothesis.alternative: Suitable may mean simply any integer, in which case the first element is suitable; it could also encode an unstated predicate.
hypothesis.reason: The specification gives no criterion for suitability or behavior when no suitable value exists, so mismatch cannot be established.

tests.reason: Without a suitability predicate, expected outputs for concrete values cannot be determined from the specification.

hypothesis.required_relation: Return a sorted copy containing every occurrence in xs.
hypothesis.actual_relation: Returns sorted(xs), which sorts all elements and retains duplicates; the temporary set does not affect the returned value.
hypothesis.alternative: The unused set assignment might suggest deduplication was intended, but it has no effect on the returned sorted list.
hypothesis.reason: The returned expression directly satisfies the stated relation for lists of integers; the unused assignment alone does not establish a mismatch.

tests.reason: A duplicate case challenges the apparent but unused set operation, while the empty list checks the boundary behavior.
